current_evidence: The council's 'Submit a planning application' page (last updated 01 April 2026) still links this Planning Application Validation Guide as the guide to plans and documents, and a web search found no newer Lancaster local list.

issues.detail: Several local list items (L1-L25) are missing from the app-type rows: L1 Affordable Housing Statement (10+ dwellings or 0.5ha+; 2+ dwellings in Arnside & Silverdale AONB; not needed in Morecambe AAP / West End Masterplan areas); L2 Air Quality Assessment (proposals in or affecting AQMAs, larger sites above thresholds, schemes that could create a new AQMA, slurry tanks or intensive livestock near designated sites); L5 Employment and Skills Plan (20+ residential units or 1,000 sq.m+ new leisure/education/commercial floorspace); L11 Hydrological Risk Assessment (all development at Port of Heysham Expansion, Port of Heysham Industrial Estate, Middleton Towers, Glasson Dock Industrial Area); L12 Land Contamination Assessment (potentially contaminated sites, within 250m of possible landfill, off-site contamination); L15 Noise & Vibration Statement; L19 Statement of Community Involvement (departures, wind schemes of more than 2 turbines or hub height over 15m, Assets of Community Value, where pre-app requires); L25 Utilities Assessment (major development or any proposal involving non-mains sewerage).
issues.evidence: PAVG Jan 2020 Section 2: e.g. L5 'An ESP will be required for all applications proposing 20 or more residential units'; L11 'All development within the following areas: ...'; L25 'A Utilities Assessment will be required for any major developments or any new proposal that involves non-mains sewerage.'

issues.detail: Several requirement names are paired with text from a different requirement. 'Design Code / Masterplan / Parameter plans' uses the West End Masterplan exemption from L1 Affordable Housing; there is no design code requirement. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' uses the tree AIA bullet list from L24. 'Telecommunications supplementary information' uses the L13 LVIA trigger, but the real L21 Telecommunications Report trigger is 'all applications proposing telecommunications equipment'. 'Ventilation / Extraction details (odour)' uses the list of measures from the L6 Energy Statement.
issues.evidence: L21: 'For all applications proposing telecommunications equipment.' L1: Morecambe AAP / West End Masterplan proposals are exempt from the AHS.

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts are fragments that do not say when the item is needed. Coal Mining ('account of land stability.') should say non-householder development in the Coal Authority Development High Risk Area. HRA ('...see 2017 Regulations on L4.') is cut off. Minerals should say all major applications partly or fully within a Mineral Safeguarding Area (L14). Drainage omits the L20 trigger: major development or 5+ residential units. Transport Assessment omits the L23 floorspace and 100+ dwelling thresholds. Archaeology gives no trigger. Health Impact Assessment is cut off mid-word ('which invol'), losing the 100+ residential units trigger. Heads of Terms is also cut off.
issues.evidence: L4 'A CMRA will be required for all applications for non-householder development'; L14 'All major applications partially or fully within a Mineral Safeguarding Area'; L20 'required for any major developments ... 5 or more residential units'.

issues.detail: 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' is placed under Householder, but the source text Grokbot quotes says householder development is exempt from the sequential test. Only the FRA itself applies to householder schemes in Flood Zones 2/3.
issues.evidence: L8: '...(though for changes of use, householder development and non-residential extensions with a footprint less than 250sq.m a sequential test will not be required)'

issues.detail: Most rows (about 23) carry 'INFERRED: placed under Full planning', and Outline, Reserved matters, Listed building, Advertisement and Prior approval are marked '(none)'. But the PAVG local list applies by development scale and location, not by consent type. For example, L24 Tree Assessment covers any proposal affecting protected trees (householder included), L10 Heritage Statement applies to LBC, and L13/L20/L23 apply to outline major applications too. Saying there are 'no local requirements' for Outline and Listed building consent is wrong.
issues.evidence: PAVG: required information 'will be dependent upon the nature and the scale of the proposed development'.

issues.detail: Some captured items are process text or fragments rather than requirements. In tab_items: the paper copy rule (merged with the 'major development' footnote) and 'The same applies to their file name if submitted electronically.' In app rows: 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' ('or where pre-application advice has specified that one is necessary' is a clause of the L18/L19 triggers, not a requirement), 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' (a citation of the EIA regulations, not its trigger), and 'Landscaping scheme' (just the AIA sub-item 'a proposed landscaping plan, which is to be included with the AIA').
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' entries; app row trigger 'or where pre-application advice has specified that one is necessary.'

issues.detail: Some rows list national (statutory) requirements as if they were local ones. Design and Access Statement is labelled as a national requirement in the source. Floor plans/elevations and the drawing standards are national list items. Meanwhile the real local items (see missing_requirement) were dropped.
issues.evidence: 'A Design and Access Statement is a national requirement for the following types of applications...'

issues.detail: The list is more than 6 years old although it says it is reviewed every two years. It still cites 'Emerging Local Plan' policies and pre-2023 NPPF paragraph numbers, and mandatory BNG or other post-2020 requirements may be missing. Grokbot's 'Outdated (>2y)? Yes' flag is right, but it is still the only list the council publishes.
issues.evidence: 'Lancaster City Council's Local List is reviewed every two years in accordance with national requirements.'

summary: The link works and is still the council's current validation guide (Jan 2020), but Grokbot's extraction is poor. Eight of the 25 local items are missing (Affordable Housing, Air Quality, Employment & Skills, Hydrological Risk, Land Contamination, Noise, SCI, Utilities), several rows are tied to another requirement's text, and almost everything is placed under Full planning by guesswork.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
